# PubMed novelty fixture screen, 25 September 2026

The [preregistered protocol](novelty-fixture-discovery-prereg-v1.json) was committed as `edca9ef7` before the three calls. The [runner](novelty_fixture_discovery.py) was committed as `1686086b`; syntax, Ruff check, and Ruff format passed. It used the maintained `pubmed_search_with_fulltext` MCP tool on a loopback server with an isolated cache, an ephemeral shared secret, no ambient credentials, and no model inference. Exactly one outer tool call was made for each frozen draft, with 1.2 seconds between calls. The [unchanged result](novelty-fixture-discovery-results-v1.json) has SHA-256 `355218115d121d3ec80a5ef1f1443f9083a30f49a0dc59ec5e4c0777ed8298bc`. All three calls returned three papers without a top-three target hit or a reported retrieval error. An outer call may make several internal ESearch attempts; this protocol capped outer calls, not the internal ladder.

They cannot serve as the positive target. |

The abstract review used the PubMed metadata saved by this isolated MCP run. The returned titles and IDs are retained in the result; the full abstract cache remains outside the repository. These judgments concern this frozen draft and these first pages, not the complete PubMed corpus. The result is a failed fixture screen, not a novelty finding and not an evaluation of result-conditioned search quality.

The code makes two plausible contributors visible: `pubmed_client.py` asks ESearch for publication-date order; `pubmed_query.py` can broaden a starved prose query to a field-tagged OR, and `literature_review.py` prefers available full text before filling with abstracts. The run did not record the chosen ESearch rung or the first nine IDs, so it does **not** establish which contributor caused these outputs. A behavioral retrieval correction and a separate, frozen post-correction screen are needed before M11-NOV-01a can accept positive cases.
